name: BQ24133RGYR
title: BQ24133: stand-alone 1- to 3-cell Li-ion 2.5 A synchronous buck charger, MOSFETs inside, with adapter/battery power-path control
summary: A switch-mode charger for one, two or three Li-ion or Li-polymer cells in series, with both buck MOSFETs inside and a fixed 1.6 MHz PWM. It charges at up to 2.5 A (10 mΩ sense resistor) to a fixed 4.2 V per cell, the cell count chosen by tying the CELL pin low, leaving it open or tying it high. It also drives an external N-channel pair between adapter and system and a P-channel FET between battery and system, so the system runs from the adapter when one is qualified and from the battery otherwise, and it trims charge current to hold total adapter current to a set limit. Input runs from 4.5 V to 17 V (30 V rated on AVCC, ACP, ACN), with an adjustable input over/undervoltage window, NTC temperature window, safety timers and battery detection, in a 24-pin 5.5 mm × 3.5 mm VQFN.
key_figures: 4.2 V, 8.4 V or 12.6 V (1, 2 or 3 cells)
80 mΩ high side, 95 mΩ low side (typ)

notes: The codes differ in reel quantity: 3000 on the large reel, 250 on the small one.

pins.name: SW
pins.function: Switch node: the junction of the internal high- and low-side MOSFETs, wired to the output inductor. The 0.047 µF bootstrap capacitor runs from this pin to BTST.

pins.name: PVCC
pins.function: Supply to the power stage. Needs a ceramic capacitor of 10 µF or more to PGND, mounted right at the pins.

pins.name: AVCC
pins.function: Supply to the control circuits. Decouple with 1 µF ceramic to AGND close to the device and feed it from the input through 10 Ω (5 Ω suggested for a 5 V input) for noise filtering.

pins.name: ACN
pins.function: Low (system) side of the adapter current sense resistor. A 0.1 µF ceramic from ACN to ACP filters the differential signal; another 0.1 µF from ACN to AGND, for common-mode filtering, is optional.

pins.name: ACP
pins.function: High (adapter) side of the adapter current sense resistor. Filtered by 0.1 µF ceramic to ACN and 0.1 µF ceramic to AGND.

pins.name: CMSRC
pins.function: Return for the input FET drive: goes through 4 kΩ to the joined sources of ACFET and RBFET, the resistor setting how fast they turn on. The total resistance between ACDRV and CMSRC must be at least 500 kΩ.

pins.name: ACDRV
pins.function: Gate drive for the back-to-back N-channel ACFET and RBFET (sources joined), through a 4 kΩ resistor. It turns the pair off fast and on slowly, and never overlaps with BATDRV (break-before-make).

pins.name: STAT
pins.function: Open-drain status output, pulled up with 10 kΩ; drives an LED or a host input. Low while charging, high when done or in SLEEP, toggling at 0.5 Hz on a fault (suspend, input overvoltage, timer fault, no battery).

pins.name: TS
pins.function: Battery temperature input for an NTC thermistor (103AT suggested). A divider from VREF through TS to AGND sets the hot and cold limits; 5 °C to 40 °C or a wider window can be set.

pins.name: TTC
pins.function: Timer and termination control. A capacitor to AGND sets the fast-charge safety timer at 5.6 min/nF (the precharge timer is a fixed 30 min). Low disables both termination and the safety timer; high disables only the timer.

pins.name: VREF
pins.function: 3.3 V reference output; decouple with 1 µF ceramic to AGND near the pin. Can supply the dividers for ISET, ACSET and TS and be the pull-up for STAT and CELL.

pins.name: ISET
pins.function: Fast-charge current set by a VREF–ISET–AGND divider: ICHG = VISET / (20 × RSR). Precharge and termination currents are one tenth of it. Below 40 mV the charger is off; above 120 mV it is on.

pins.name: CELL
pins.function: Cell count at 4.2 V per cell: low for 1 cell, open (0.8 V to 1.8 V) for 2 cells, high for 3 cells.

pins.name: SRN
pins.function: Battery side of the charge current sense resistor. Filter with 0.1 µF ceramic to SRP and 0.1 µF ceramic to AGND.

pins.name: SRP
pins.function: Inductor side of the charge current sense resistor. Filter with 0.1 µF ceramic to SRN and 0.1 µF ceramic to AGND.

pins.name: ACSET
pins.function: Input (DPM) current limit set by a VREF–ACSET–AGND divider: IDPM = VACSET / (20 × RAC).

pins.name: OVPSET
pins.function: Input voltage window, from a divider between the input and AGND. Above the internal 1.6 V reference the input is over voltage; below 0.5 V it is under voltage. Either one stops charge, opens ACFET/RBFET and sets STAT blinking.

pins.name: BATDRV
pins.function: Gate drive, through 1 kΩ, for the P-channel BATFET whose source sits on the system node and drain on the battery positive. Fast off, slow on, and break-before-make against ACDRV.

pins.name: REGN
pins.function: 6 V supply output for the low-side driver; needs 1 µF ceramic to PGND near the device. Feeds BTST through the internal bootstrap diode.

pins.name: BTST
pins.function: Supply to the high-side driver; the 0.047 µF bootstrap capacitor connects from SW to this pin.

pins.name: PGND
pins.function: Ground of the power stage. Wire straight to the ground of the input and output capacitors; join AGND only through the thermal pad under the device.

pins.name: AGND
pins.function: Exposed pad: analog ground and the heat path. Always solder it down, with vias to the ground plane, as the single star point between analog and power ground.

circuits.title: Typical application: 12 V input, 2 cells, 2 A charge
circuits.description: A 12 V adapter feeds the system through the back-to-back N-channel pair Q1 (ACFET) and Q2 (RBFET), whose joined sources go to CMSRC through R12 and whose gates go to ACDRV through R11; the 20 mΩ resistor RAC after them senses adapter current on ACP and ACN. When the adapter is gone, the P-channel Q3, driven from BATDRV through R14, ties the battery to the system. The buck stage runs from SW through 3.3 µH and the 10 mΩ resistor RSR to the battery, with C5 as bootstrap capacitor. R2/R3 from VREF set ISET to about 0.40 V (2 A charge, 0.2 A precharge and termination); R4/R5 set ACSET for a 2 A input limit; R6/R7 put the input overvoltage trip near 18 V. CELL is left open for 2 cells (8.4 V), R8/R9 with the 103AT thermistor set a 0 °C to 45 °C window, C3 sets the safety timer, and D3 with R10 shows status. AVCC is fed through R1 from the adapter or the battery by the diode pair D1/D2. RIN and CIN damp the input.
notes: Design targets: 12 V input, 8.4 V (2 cells), 2 A charge, 0.2 A precharge and termination, 2 A input limit, 18 V input overvoltage, 0 °C to 45 °C.
CELL is unconnected (open) to select 2 cells.

circuits.title: Single-cell non-removable battery, USB or adapter input
circuits.description: A one-cell version with the system tied to the inductor side of the charge sense resistor, so no BATFET is used and BATDRV is left open; with a fixed battery the cell can carry the system when the adapter is overloaded. One N-channel FET, Q4, blocks reverse current from the system to the input. CELL and TTC are grounded (1 cell; termination and safety timer off). R2/R3 from VREF set ISET. The input limit is 2 A from R4/R5A, or about 500 mA when the ILIM_500mA signal turns on the small N-channel FET and puts R5B in parallel with R5A. R6/R7 trip the input overvoltage near 15 V; R8/R9 with the 103AT set a 5 °C to 40 °C window. D1 from REGN to BTST is optional. AVCC is fed from the input through R11 (5 Ω).

parts.note: gate resistor, ACDRV to Q4 gate

notes: Design targets: input overvoltage 15 V, up to 2 A charge, 0.2 A precharge, 2 A adapter or 500 mA USB input limit, 5 °C to 40 °C.

circuits.title: Typical application with a diode in the adapter path
circuits.description: A simpler front end: the adapter reaches the system through a series diode D1 instead of an N-channel FET pair, and the adapter sense resistor RAC follows it. The P-channel BATFET Q1, driven from BATDRV through R11, connects the battery to the system. The buck stage runs from SW through L1 and RSR to the battery pack. Divider R1/R2 from VREF sets ACSET and R3/R4 sets ISET; R6/R7 from the adapter set the OVPSET window; R9/R10 with the thermistor RTH set the TS window; C6 sets the safety timer; D2 through R8 shows status. AVCC is fed through R5 from the adapter or the battery by a pair of diodes. CELL is left open (2 cells).

circuits.title: TS resistor network
circuits.description: RT1 from VREF to TS and RT2 from TS to ground, with the 103AT thermistor on the battery pack in parallel with RT2, scale the thermistor voltage onto the TS thresholds. For a 0 °C to 45 °C window the worked values are RT1 = 5.23 kΩ and RT2 = 30.1 kΩ (thermistor 27.28 kΩ cold, 4.911 kΩ hot).

parts.note: NTC thermistor on the battery pack

circuits.title: Input filter against hot-plug overshoot
circuits.description: Protects AVCC from the ringing of cable inductance against the input capacitor when an adapter is plugged in. R1 (2 Ω, 2010 size) in series with C1 (2.2 µF) across the adapter damps the ringing. D1 blocks reverse input voltage. R2 (4.7 Ω to 30 Ω, 1206 size) and C2 (0.1 µF to 1 µF, at the AVCC pin) form a second RC that slows fast edges into AVCC. C2 is kept smaller than C1. With a 5 V USB input D1 can be omitted, and R2 must then be at least 5 Ω to limit current if the input is plugged in reversed.

circuits.title: Input ACFET and RBFET with turn-on slowing
circuits.description: The N-channel pair Q1 (ACFET, drain to the adapter) and Q2 (RBFET, drain toward the system) with sources joined. CGD across Q1 drain to gate, and CGS with the 499 kΩ RGS across gate to source, slow Q1's turn-on to limit the inrush into the capacitance on PVCC (about 10 µF at the charger and 40 µF on the system). R11 (4.02 kΩ) links the gates to ACDRV and R12 (4.02 kΩ) the sources to CMSRC. One evaluation design uses 4.7 nF CGD and 47 nF CGS with a CSD17313 as Q1.

operation.text: A charge has three stages: precharge at one tenth of the set current while the cell is below VLOWV, then constant current at the ISET value, then constant voltage at 4.2 V per cell until current falls to the termination level. Precharge is timed by a fixed 30 min timer and fast charge by the TTC timer.
CELL sets the regulation voltage: tied to AGND gives 4.2 V, left open 8.4 V, tied to VREF 12.6 V.

ISET up to 0.5 V sets the fast-charge current. ISET below 40 mV turns the charger off and above 120 mV turns it on. With 10 mΩ, set more than 600 mA. At high temperature the current is reduced to keep the die at 120 °C.

If the battery starts below VLOWV the charger applies 10 % of the fast-charge current to recover a deeply flat cell. If VLOWV is not reached within 30 min the charger stops and STAT reports a fault. Moving between precharge and fast charge has a 25 ms deglitch.

Adapter current is the system load plus charge input. When their sum would pass the ACSET limit, the charger lowers its own current, so the adapter can be sized for less than both peaks together. RAC is normally 20 mΩ; a larger value gives more signal and accuracy for more loss.

In the voltage stage, charge ends when SRN is above the recharge threshold and current is below ITERM. A new cycle starts when the battery falls below the recharge threshold, on power-on reset, or when ISET is taken below 40 mV and back above 120 mV. TTC tied to AGND disables termination and the fast-charge timer (and resets the timer); TTC tied to VREF disables only the timer.

AVCC can be powered from the adapter or the battery, so a comparator decides the source. With AVCC above SRN the device leaves SLEEP and, if every condition is met, charges. With SRN above AVCC it enters a low-current SLEEP mode in which VREF is off and STAT is high impedance. Below UVLO the device is off.
Below the UVLO threshold on AVCC all circuits are off. AVCC can be held up by the battery through the high-side MOSFET body diode.
When OVPSET rises above 1.6 V (ACOV) or falls below 0.5 V (ACUV), charge stops and the input FETs turn off. The divider from the input to OVPSET sets the accepted input window.

Charge runs only with ISET above 120 mV, AVCC above UVLO and above SRN, OVPSET between 0.5 V and 1.6 V, the 1.5 s start-up delay over, REGN and VREF in regulation, no thermal shutdown, no TS fault and ACFET on. Any of these failing, or a timer expiring, stops charge.

The battery feeds the system by default at power-up and in SLEEP: BATDRV sits at ACN - 6 V (clamped at ground) while AVCC is above UVLO and ACN is below SRN + 200 mV. Once the device leaves SLEEP with AVCC at least 300 mV above SRN and OVPSET inside the window, both FETs are held off for 10 µs, BATDRV is pulled to ACN, and a charge pump raises ACDRV to CMSRC + 6 V to turn ACFET on. When the adapter is removed ACFET turns off, SLEEP is entered, and BATFET turns on once the system has fallen near SRN. RBFET stops the battery discharging back into the input; ACFET's turn-on time limits dI/dt into the system. The gate drives turn off fast and on slowly; a gate-to-source capacitor lengthens the delay.

A fixed 1.6 MHz synchronous buck with internal type III compensation, which allows ceramic output capacitors. The PWM ramp height scales with AVCC to keep loop gain constant over input voltage. Duty cycle reaches 97 % before pulses are skipped.
Every entry into fast charge ramps the current target up in eight equal steps of about 1.6 ms each, about 12.8 ms in all, with no external parts.

The high-side MOSFET current is sensed and the switch is held open until the next cycle once it passes its limit. A second limit stops charge current exceeding 160 % of the set value. Both recover by themselves once current is below the threshold.

When SRP-SRN falls below 5 mV the low-side FET stays off until the next cycle, so the inductor current cannot reverse and boost energy back onto the input and AVCC. In DCM the low-side FET is briefly turned on to refresh the bootstrap capacitor when it falls below 4 V.

On power-up, or when the battery falls below the recharge threshold, an 8 mA sink is applied to SRN for up to 1 s. If SRN falls below LOWV the sink is removed and a 125 mA charge is applied for up to 0.5 s; if SRN then rises above the recharge threshold no battery is present and the test repeats. If either timer runs out first, a battery is present and charge begins. Capacitance on the battery node must be small enough for the 8 mA sink to pull it below LOWV within 1 s.
With SRN below 2 V during charge, the charger stops for 1 ms and then soft-starts again at the precharge current, running non-synchronously, so the inductor cannot saturate into a shorted battery.

The high-side FET is held off until the battery falls below 102 % of the regulation voltage, giving a one-cycle response to load removal or battery disconnect. A 6 mA sink from SRP/SRN to AGND removes the energy left in the inductor. If the overvoltage lasts more than 30 ms, charge is disabled.

The TS voltage, from an NTC and divider, is compared with internal thresholds. To start a charge the temperature must lie between VLTF and VHTF; during charge it must lie between VLTF and VTCO. Outside the window the PWM is stopped until the temperature returns between VLTF and VHTF.

Cycle-by-cycle monitoring of the MOSFET drop catches shorts. The charger latches off while ACFET stays on to supply the system, and STAT blinks; only removing and replugging the adapter clears the latch.
Charge current is reduced to hold the junction at 120 °C. Above 150 °C the converter shuts down, and it restarts when the junction cools below 130 °C.

If a time-out happens with the battery above the recharge threshold, the fault clears when the battery falls below it, and battery detection starts. If the battery is below the threshold, a small fault current is applied until the battery rises above it, then the first case applies. A power-on reset or ISET below 40 mV also clears the fault.
STAT is open drain: on while charging, off when done, in SLEEP or disabled, and blinking on suspend, input or battery overvoltage, timer fault or missing battery.

The device runs the system from a qualified adapter or from the battery, and stops the battery boosting back into the input. External circuits can change ISET or ACSET while running, for example to switch input limits or to enable a battery learn cycle.
At 1.6 MHz small L and C values are usable. Choose saturation current above the charge current plus half the ripple; ripple is designed for 20 % to 40 % of maximum charge current.

Needs a ripple current rating for up to half the charge current. Use low-ESR X7R or X5R ceramic placed close to the high-side drain and low-side source; 25 V or higher for a 15 V input; about 20 µF for 2.5 A charge.
Ceramic X7R or X5R rated 25 V or more. Choose L and C for a resonance between 15 kHz and 25 kHz; Typical pairs are 6.8 µH with 10 µF for 1 A and 3.3 µH with 20 µF for 2 A.

When an adapter is plugged in, cable inductance and the input capacitor ring and can push AVCC past its rating. A high-ESR electrolytic or a TVS diode will limit it; a smaller, cheaper option is an RC snubber across the input plus a series RC into AVCC. Size R1 and R2 for the inrush power and confirm values in the real application.
About 50 µF sits on the PVCC node (10 µF at the charger, 40 µF on the system), so ACFET's turn-on causes a surge. Choose a FET with larger CGD and CGS, or add external capacitors, to slow it.
The input supply should be 4.5 V to 17 V and preferably able to deliver more than 500 mA.

In order: keep the input capacitor tight to PVCC and ground on the same layer, without vias; put the inductor right at SW with a small but current-capable copper area on one layer, away from other traces; put RSR next to the inductor output and route the SRP/SRN sense lines as a Kelvin pair on one layer, away from high-current paths, with their filter capacitors next to the device; place the output capacitor next to RSR and ground; join output and input capacitor grounds before system ground; keep analog ground apart from power ground and join them once at the thermal pad (or with a 0 Ω resistor), star fashion; solder the thermal pad with enough vias to the ground plane; put decoupling capacitors at the pins; size vias for the current.
